tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Implement the 24 In Plain Sight recommendations as a coordinated health-system response.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: B.C. Ministry of Health with Indigenous partners and health-system organizations
tracked_items.expected_implementation_date: Task Team mandate through 2023; continuing work after mandate
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The 24-month report documented work on multiple recommendations. Later provincial material says the Task Team concluded in June 2023 and implementation continues, while the Ministry acknowledges work remains and identifies capacity and competing-priority risks.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: No source supports treating all 24 recommendations as complete; continuing implementation is not a contradiction.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Adopt an Indigenous cultural-safety and humility accreditation standard across health policy-makers, authorities, regulators, facilities and education programs.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: B.C. Ministry of Health, First Nations Health Authority, Health Standards Organization and health-system partners
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The BC Cultural Safety and Humility Standard was released in 2022. Later action-status material says it guides organizations and that work continues toward its first assessment/accreditation use; it does not establish organization-wide adoption.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Standard release is demonstrated; full adoption and effect are not.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Extend public-interest disclosure protections so health-sector employees can report Indigenous-specific racism and other concerns.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The provincial action-status page reports Public Interest Disclosure Act protections were extended to health-authority employees. This demonstrates the legal protection, not reporting rates or safety outcomes.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: No outcome evaluation located.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Embed anti-discrimination and Indigenous cultural-safety expectations in professional regulation and complaint accountability.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Government of British Columbia and health regulatory colleges
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The Health Professions and Occupations Act is in force and identifies discrimination as actionable professional conduct. The available source describes implementation work as underway and does not demonstrate all college-level operational changes or outcomes.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Legal enactment should not be read as proof of consistent regulatory practice.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Carry out BCCDC leadership commitments following its 2025 apology, including work toward eliminating Indigenous-specific racism.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The BCCDC source records commitments and frames the apology as a beginning. No later public progress report or outcome evidence was located in this pass.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Absence of later public evidence is not evidence of non-implementation.
tracked_items.owner_review_reason: A later organization-level implementation update or evaluation is needed before treating commitments as underway or complete.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Establish a health anti-racism and cultural-safety centre under the provincial anti-racism action plan.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The benchmark’s 2026 government release documents the commitment. No operating-centre evidence or outcome report was located in this pass.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Announcement alone is not implementation.
tracked_items.owner_review_reason: Confirm centre establishment, mandate, funding, and public service availability before upgrading status.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Create a culturally grounded, responsive Indigenous complaints pathway and alternative accountability process.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Fraser Salish Region, First Nations Health Authority and Fraser Health
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The FNHA 2024-25 annual report describes an Indigenous-led unified complaints pathway being implemented with Fraser Health, replacing fragmented systems and identifying systemic patterns. It does not provide completion or effectiveness measures.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Local implementation is evidenced; province-wide availability is not claimed.
tracked_items.repeat_signal_detail: The 2025 FNHA service plan continues to identify transforming the complaints model as a regional priority; this supports ongoing work, not non-implementation.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Make patient safety and patient-care-quality review processes more open and culturally safe when harm, including Indigenous-specific racism, is alleged.
tracked_items.expected_implementation_date: policy and legislative direction after 2026 engagement
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The Ministry’s 2026 engagement reviewed internal patient-safety and patient-care-quality processes, with consultations intended to refine policy direction and support future legislative changes. It did not report completed policy reform.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Review and engagement are not evidence that complaint reforms are operational.
tracked_items.repeat_signal_detail: The 2026 review revisits the 2020 concern about culturally unsafe quality-review processes, suggesting the policy problem remains actively unresolved.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Implement the Calgary Zone Indigenous Health Action Plan’s five pillars, including culturally safe care, complaint-process improvement and shared accountability.
tracked_items.expected_implementation_date: phased over the life of the plan
tracked_items.evidence_summary: AHS’s 2023-24 annual report records Calgary Zone implementation activity including operational committee meetings, a Zone Eliminating Racism Working Group and regular partnership discussions. It does not report pillar-by-pillar completion or outcomes.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Activity evidence is not plan-wide completion evidence.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Implement the Indigenous Primary Health Care Advisory Panel’s 22 recommendations through five actionable outcomes.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: Alberta’s implementation page says several actions are completed or underway, including creation of an Indigenous Health Division and an Indigenous Patient Complaints Investigator. It expressly does not establish completion of all 22 recommendations.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: The source supports partial, not complete, implementation.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Create an Indigenous Health Division to incorporate First Nation, Métis and Inuit priorities into provincial health policy, legislation, programs and services.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Government of Alberta Ministry of Primary and Preventative Health Services
tracked_items.evidence_summary: Alberta’s implementation page states that an Indigenous Health Division has been created. It does not provide outcome measures for the division’s policy impact.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Creation is documented; effectiveness remains unmeasured in the located source.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Create an Indigenous Patient Navigator Grant Program to improve culturally safe navigation and support.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The benchmark government update documents program creation, but this pass did not locate a grantee list, service-availability measure or outcomes report.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: A program announcement is not evidence that navigator services are operating at scale.
tracked_items.owner_review_reason: Verify funded recipients and service availability before treating the program as implemented.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Operate an Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate to receive concerns, make recommendations and advise government and health authorities.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The provincial program page describes the Investigator and Advocate’s mandate and public access role. Individual matter outcomes are confidential and no outcome evaluation was located.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Service availability is documented; effectiveness should not be inferred from the office’s existence.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Use Indigenous health-care anti-racism engagement to develop a later strategy or corrective actions.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The benchmark recorded engagement results as under review. This pass did not locate a later final strategy, implementation plan or progress report attributable to that engagement.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: No clear public follow-up was located; this is not a finding of non-implementation.
tracked_items.owner_review_reason: A post-engagement government response is needed to establish whether commitments proceeded.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: CPSA will carry out its Path to Truth and Reconciliation, including an apology, standards/policies, training and partner engagement.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta
tracked_items.evidence_summary: CPSA reports early Path actions, 2025 engagement and a planned Standard of Practice implementation in 2026. Its own material describes the work as multi-year and does not claim completed standards, training or outcomes.

status_sources.organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta
College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta

tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Work underway and a future standard date are consistent; neither proves regulated-member training or practice change.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Maintain an Indigenous Advisory Circle and formalize collaboration with G4 Health on Indigenous health priorities.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta and G4 Health
tracked_items.evidence_summary: CPSA’s 2025 annual report documents the formal G4 Health relationship and identifies the Indigenous Advisory Circle as the guide for this work. It does not claim downstream patient outcomes.

status_sources.organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta

tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Partnership formation is documented; its effectiveness is not yet established.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Implement the Indigenous Human Rights Strategy external-review recommendations to reduce barriers and make Commission services culturally relevant.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The Commission reports an Indigenous Advisory Circle, integration of Indigenous practices/customs in complaints and tribunal processes, ongoing staff training, and recruitment efforts. No complete recommendation-by-recommendation report was located.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Documented initiatives do not establish full external-review implementation or accessibility outcomes.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Complete the reported Alberta Health Services quality-assurance review and follow-up communication after the Strathmore complaint.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The original reporting described a quality-assurance review. This pass did not locate a public review result, implementation response, human-rights decision or settlement.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: No public outcome located; allegations remain unadjudicated in the reviewed sources.
tracked_items.owner_review_reason: A primary AHS or tribunal source is required before attributing any outcome or corrective action.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Implement the 2017 tubal-ligation review’s calls to action on consent, cultural safety, reproductive rights and prevention of recurrence.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Saskatoon Health Region; Saskatchewan Health Authority successor
tracked_items.evidence_summary: SHA explicitly links the Indigenous Birth Support Worker Program to the 2017 report, and the program has operated since 2019. Located sources do not provide a plan-wide accounting of all calls to action.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: A linked service shows partial response, not completion of all calls to action.
tracked_items.repeat_signal_detail: The program evaluation calls for expansion to other locations and stronger partnerships, suggesting the documented response was local rather than fully system-wide.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Operate the Indigenous Birth Support Worker Program as a culturally responsive pregnancy, birth and postpartum service.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Saskatchewan Health Authority and Jim Pattison Children’s Hospital
tracked_items.evidence_summary: SHA reports the program was implemented in December 2019, evaluated after one year, served 1,023 registered clients from December 2019 to January 2021, and remains listed as a free service at Jim Pattison Children’s Hospital.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: This demonstrates operation of one local service, not causal outcome measurement or province-wide availability.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Proposed class action sought legal accountability for reported coerced tubal ligations.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Court process; named defendants in pleadings
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The benchmark sources document a proposed class action. This pass did not locate a verified certification decision, settlement, judgment or current court status.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: A legal filing is not an implementation claim or adjudicated result.
tracked_items.owner_review_reason: Court-record verification is required before describing the legal process as resolved.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Create and operate a First Nations-led health ombudsperson office to receive complaints, support resolution and recommend system change.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Federation of Sovereign Indigenous Nations First Nations Health Ombudsperson Office
tracked_items.evidence_summary: Federal funding material established the office, and the current office website confirms an active complaint and accountability function. Public case outcomes are not assumed from the office’s existence.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Office operation is evidenced; effectiveness and individual outcomes remain separate questions.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Provide mediated remedies: compensation, apology and employee training intended to eliminate systemic racism.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The Saskatchewan Human Rights Commission reports compensation, a letter of apology, and an agreement to employee training. It does not publish confirmation that training was delivered, who received it, or its effect.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Do not infer training completion from a mediated agreement.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Roll out the SHA Systemic and Indigenous-specific Anti-Racism Framework and Action Plan with monitoring.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: SHA reports the framework was developed, assessed during Accreditation Canada’s 2024 visit, and was commended; surveyors encouraged a monitoring plan. A later government page says it will be rolled out to staff.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Development and assessment are evidenced; monitoring and full roll-out remain incomplete or unclear.
tracked_items.repeat_signal_detail: Accreditation surveyors’ later call for a monitoring plan is a closely related follow-up signal, not proof of non-implementation.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Deliver mandatory cultural-responsiveness and Indigenous-specific anti-racism training to SHA staff.
tracked_items.evidence_summary: SHA reports its mandatory course launched in January 2024 and 81% of staff had completed it by March 31, 2025. It also reports in-person systemic and Indigenous-specific anti-racism training was developed for delivery beginning May 2025.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: The 81% figure proves partial completion, not all-staff training completion or effectiveness.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Conduct an independent province-wide hospital safety and protective-services review and use it to identify improvements.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Saskatchewan Ministry of Health and Saskatchewan Health Authority
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The official launch says the review will include First Nations and Métis organizations, examine current practices and recommend improvements. It also documents interim metal-detector and third-party-security actions. The review expressly excludes detailed investigations of individual incidents and no final report was located.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Interim security measures are not evidence that the independent review’s recommendations were adopted.

tracked_items.recommendation_or_commitment: Consider First Nations Health Ombudsperson recommendations submitted to the hospital safety and security review.
tracked_items.responsible_organization: Saskatchewan Ministry of Health, Saskatchewan Health Authority and review team
tracked_items.evidence_summary: The benchmark’s independent report documents submission of recommendations. This pass did not locate an official response, acceptance decision, final review report or implementation update.
tracked_items.contradiction_or_conflict_notes: Submission alone is not acceptance or implementation.
tracked_items.owner_review_reason: Verify the primary submission and government/review-team response before connecting recommendations to implementation.

proposed_model_extension.reason: One accountability action can contain multiple materially distinct recommendations with different responsible organizations, timelines, scopes and implementation evidence; the existing action-level recommendations text and one implementation status cannot represent that cleanly.
proposed_model_extension.proposal: Add a private child model named miller_north_accountability_commitments, linked to one accountability action, with commitment_id, neutral_summary, responsible_organization, commitment_date, expected_completion_date, implementation_status, implementation_status_date, implementation_evidence_summary, implementation_scope, conflict_notes, follow_up_due_date, owner_review_flag/reason, provenance and timestamps. Retain existing action-level fields as a roll-up only.
proposed_model_extension.deployment: proposal only; no migration was created or applied in this pass
